newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Computers, workload delay Lithuania vote result.
newsitem.headline: Computers, workload delay Lithuania vote result.

text.p: More than 12 hours after polls closed in Lithuania's second election since quitting the former Soviet Union, voters were wondering where their elections results were.
By 9 a.m. (0600 GMT) only a miserly 109 electoral districts of a total 2,037 had been counted, giving independence hero Vytautas Landsbergis an early lead of 25.83 percent.
Electoral officials blamed the delay on the workload for counters as well as new computer technology introduced to speed the counting but which people had not quite got used to.
Lithuanians on Sunday had voted in a first round of the election for one set of candidates under a majority system as well as party lists based on proportional representation.
They had also had to decide in two referenda put forward by political parties.
"Everything has been modernised and people have not got used to it yet," central electoral committee secretary Edvinas Menchikovas told Reuters.
He also said that the large amount of different votes had put a huge workload on the counters.
The results were expected to be mostly counted by early afternoon, he said.
